instructions:
You are the need-analysis step of an operational agent. The principal wrote one sentence. Decide
whether they want to know something (information), to have an ability they will keep using (tool), or to have
something done once (action). Decide
what information (or ability) they actually need, without choosing any implementation, provider, tool,
metric source or architecture. Identify the subjects exactly as written. For each question, define the quantity
precisely enough that two engineers would count the same thing, including who must be excluded for the answer to
be true to the principal's words, and which time windows make it meaningful. State which forms of answer are
honest when an exact count is impossible. Choose the deliverable form from the wording (e.g. 'at a glance' means
a view readable in seconds that stays current). For tool and action needs list requirements: what must be
possible, each with an observable acceptance check, tied to the words it comes from; questions may then be empty.

payload.sentence: I want to know, at a glance, how many real people are actually using LindyBooks.

handled_as.description: software_capability: satisfying this needs some software to observe, compute, present or act on something; housing: finding a place to live; other: neither

as_written.description: the exact words in the sentence

windows.description: time windows that make the answer meaningful, e.g. 24h, 7d, 30d, all_time

deliver_at_local.description: HH:MM local time if the wording implies when to be told (e.g. 'every morning')

need_type.description: information: wants to know something; tool: wants an ability they keep using (an app, a place to do X); action: wants something done once

requirements.description: for tool and action needs: what must be possible, each with an observable acceptance check

from_words.description: the words in the sentence this comes from

definitions_to_state.description: ambiguities the answer must resolve explicitly

questions.question: How many distinct real human people have actually used LindyBooks recently?
questions.quantity: Distinct individual humans who performed at least one meaningful use action (e.g. opened and engaged with the product beyond signing up or loading a page) in the window; each person counted once across devices/accounts where identifiable
questions.population: Real human end users of LindyBooks who engaged in meaningful use during the window
exclude: internal staff, developers and test/demo accounts
duplicate accounts or devices of the same person where detectable
anonymous one-off page loads with no real engagement

questions.question: How does the count of actively-using real people compare to total registered accounts?
questions.quantity: Total registered accounts, for context against active real people

deliverable.why: 'At a glance' implies a view readable in seconds that stays current, showing one headline number of real active people.

definitions_to_state: What 'using' means: which action counts as meaningful use (not just signup or page load)
What 'real people' means: humans excluding bots, staff, test and duplicate accounts
Time window for 'using' (default e.g. 30 days active, with 24h and 7d alongside)
Unit of a person: how identity is resolved across devices/accounts, and how unidentifiable anonymous visitors are handled
Whether the number is exact or an estimate/lower bound, with the confidence stated
What 'LindyBooks' refers to (which product/site/app, and whether the principal owns it) — unknown
output.success_looks_like: A single headline number of distinct real humans actively using LindyBooks in a stated window, visible in seconds, kept current, with the definition and any estimate caveat labelled.
